The reviewer also thought the card's typeface changed between frames; it is the same face (Outfit) throughout, checked in close-up. The published version was not re-scored. topic: Zoom in on your logo: squares or curves? Squares means a JPG or a PNG, which is only a picture, so a bigger picture means bigger squares. Curves means a vector file (SVG, AI or EPS), sharp on a pen and on the side of a van. Ask whoever made your logo for it.

topic: Limited company? Those three letters come with a list. A limited company's website has to show four things: the registered number, the registered office address, where the company is registered, and the fact that it is a limited company (GOV.UK, Running a limited company). Shown as the end of a brass nameplate for a made-up company, Kittiwake & Quay Ltd, then LTD close up, then a second plate with the four as four engraved lines. Check your footer tonight.
text_font: Outfit (headlines and footer); Newsreader capitals engraved on the plates
reason: First held by the scheduled run at 6.5 twice (frame 3, two stacked plates, called basic). Reworked the same evening when Lee asked for it to be posted.
design_review_note: Round 1 (6.5; frames 6.5, 5.5, 7): the plate drawn in CSS with blur and bevel filters, Anton headlines. Faults named: 'a faux-3D effect, not a photograph or a proper render', the close-up of LTD soft like an upscale with clipped letters above it, the condensed headline face reading as a template, two question marks stacked, headlines at two sizes, a plate that changed between frames, a company number of all zeros, background streaks. Round 2 (6.5; frames 7, 7, 5.5) was rebuilt from nothing: each plate face drawn flat and placed by a small camera in Python (true perspective, sides, shadows), letters cut with a lighting filter in an engraver's serif, Outfit headlines at one size, no blur, a flat gloss door. Frame 1 was called the boldest and frame 2 the cleanest. Frame 3's faults: name cropped mid-word, the two plates in slightly different perspective, the gloss stripe through LTD, plates 40px apart, the lower plate's edge lining up with nothing, the last engraved line near the screws, small engraving that looks printed, 'all four' not shown as four. Across the set: the same two-stripe gloss on every plate reads as an effect, the brass is too even, 'Kittiwake' unreadable at the far end of frame 1, tight headline tracking. Not re-scored and not patched after round 2. Rework after Lee's message. Round 3 (6.5; frames 5.5, 7.5, 6.5): frame 3 rebuilt as one long tilted plate with the four things as four lines, a different reflection on each plate, the door view eased so the whole name could be read. Faults named: frame 1's name still crushed at the far end and a blown-out band of light at the near end; the camera flipping sides between frames 1 and 2; blotchy brass on frame 3; the footer low. Round 4 (6.5; frames 6.5, 7.5, 6): frame 1 rebuilt from the same side as frame 2 (QUAY LTD and the plate end, so frame 2 is a push-in), one strip of sky as the reflection on every plate, the blotches removed, the footer lifted. Faults named: frame 3's small lines too widely word-spaced and its screws close to the text, the plate on frame 2 starting at the header line, the Q on frame 1 just off the margin, a brown shadow. Those were fixed before publishing (word spacing back to normal and the lines a size up, a taller plate with the screws clear, frame 2's plate lowered, the Q on the margin, the shadow a deep red) and it was not scored again. Not fixed: the reviewers' ceiling, that frame 3 is a second plate and its small print is small.
